knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Debris is removed gradually and the volume recorded, which avoids disturbing the pond's balance in one visit.
Sludge and discharge routes must be confirmed against local council and water rules before any water is moved.
Wild plants may be protected or declared, and removing them from the wild can be prohibited.

practicalCriteria: Learner completes procedure step 1: Read the owner's plan for the visit, including any leaf-season arrangement and any agreed litter area.
Learner completes procedure step 2: Remove floating debris with a net, working from the edge inward, and avoid stirring the sediment.
Learner completes procedure step 3: Clean the skimmer basket and the pre-filter, with the pump isolated before any part is opened.
Learner completes procedure step 4: Measure the sediment depth at the reference point and remove sludge in layers, using as little water as possible.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 4: Measure the sediment depth at the reference point and remove sludge in layers, using as little water as possible.
Record of procedure step 6: Trim or remove rotting plant matter, check the plant baskets, and keep floating plants within the agreed area.
Record of procedure step 7: Record the volumes, material types, time taken and any water movement, and wear the PPE set by {{business:safety.required_ppe}}.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 3 is not done: Clean the skimmer basket and the pre-filter, with the pump isolated before any part is opened.
Stop work if procedure step 4 is not done: Measure the sediment depth at the reference point and remove sludge in layers, using as little water as possible.
